description: We are students from aou and kau collaborating to bring a solution for a complete Martian Guide. Through NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are developing NEXUS-MARS, an interactive Martian exploration and survival platform that transforms real NASA data into an engaging tool for understanding and navigating the Red Planet. Welcoming interested members.
summary: Nexus Mars is an interactive web-based Martian Survival Guide developed in response to NASA's challenge of creating an integrated map to support future human exploration of Mars. It combines 2D and 3D Martian maps with layered environmental data, including surface temperature, terrain, slopes, and potential hazards, bringing information from NASA's Mars exploration resources into one platform. Users can explore selected regions, identify safer routes, examine destinations, and plan Marswalks through drone scouting, rover navigation, and astronaut simulation modes. The platform also aims to estimate travel distance, time, and oxygen requirements to support mission planning. By transforming complex Martian geographical and scientific data into an accessible, interactive guide, Nexus Mars aims to help future astronauts make informed decisions, minimize exploration risks, and conduct safer and more efficient scientific missions on the Martian surface.
details:
1- It is an interactive website, to simulate Martian terrain, safe routes and environmental conditions.

2- It provides environmental and geographical data of Mars for first human expedition including the use of drone for scouting the area, reducing risks and making it a safer expedition.

3- It supports safer, smarter and more efficient future human expedition of Mars.

4- It uses HTML, JavaScript and CSS. It also utilities the NASA resources provided. For hardware it uses Raspberry pi 5 as it's brain, NRF24L01 for communication, TFT- LCD for display.

5- It combines 2D and 3D mapping, environmental analysis, includes 3 exploration modes and mission planning under one platform

6- We considered terrain, slopes, temperature, geographical hazards, travel distance, time oxygen consumption, and communication reliability
